key_insight: Snoring audio contains measurable patterns that can distinguish palatal from epiglottic upper-airway obstruction in OSA with high accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a non-invasive, audio-based screening tool could help localize obstruction and complement DISE when planning OSA care.
method: 159 DISE recordings from adults with moderate, non-positional OSA
Snoring events were expertly labeled for palatal vs epiglottic origin using only fully agreed cases
Acoustic features were fed into SVM and MLP models with patient-independent nested cross-validation
evidence_signal: Using 1,759 snoring events, both models achieved ROC AUC 0.90 ± 0.03, with balanced accuracy of 0.83 for SVM and 0.81 for MLP.
watch_item: Results came from retrospective DISE recordings in a specific OSA subgroup, so broader real-world validation and standardized recording conditions are still needed.
paper_title: The sound of snoring: AI-based acoustic phenotyping of upper airway obstruction in Obstructive Sleep Apnea
